summary: Richard G. Salomon works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied under Ludo Rocher (~1970–1975) and served at the University of Washington as Professor (~1981–2019) and later Emeritus Professor (~2019), and at Soka University in 2007.

Richard Gombrich is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Oxford (BA ~1957–1961, DPhil ~1965–1970) and under Gananath Obeyesekere, K. R. Norman, and Walpola Rahula. He held professorships at Oxford (1965–2004) and Balliol College (1976–2004).

Richard Hartshorne studied at Princeton University (~1916–1920) and the University of Chicago (~1920–1924). He held posts at the University of Minnesota (~1924–1940) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1940–1970).

Richard Hauschild worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Jena (PhD ~1920–1926, Habilitation by 1948), Tübingen, and Leipzig, studying under Albert Debrunner and Johannes Hertel. He was a lecturer, PD, and professor at the University of Jena (1938–1967).

Linguist Richard Henebry studied at St. John's College, Waterford (~1882–1884), St Patrick's Pontifical University, Maynooth (~1884–1892), the University of Greifswald under Heinrich Zimmer (~1896–1898), and the University of Freiburg (~1898).

Richard Hugh Robinson worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned degrees at Alberta, SOAS, and the University of London, studying under Arthur Waley, David Friedman, David Snellgrove, and Edward Conze. He taught at Wisconsin-Madison from 1960 until 1970.

Richard Hughes Seager specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Wisconsin System, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University (PhD ~1982–1987). Around 1994, he was Associate Professor of Religion at Hamilton College.

Philosopher Richard Hönigswald studied at the University of Vienna (~1893–1899), the University of Graz, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1902–1904). He held posts at the University of Breslau (1906–1930) and the University of Munich (1930–1933).

Richard J. Davidson studied at New York University (BA 1968–1972) and Harvard University (PhD 1972–1976). He has held multiple roles at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, including Professor from 1987 and Director (2001–2017).

Richard Jay Kohn was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1988, studying under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundup Sopa and traditional teacher Lama Tharchin Rinpoche.

Richard K. Payne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Chisei Aratano and Taisen Miyata. He served as Dean at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1993–2017) and on the Graduate Theological Union faculty (~2003).

Linguist Richard Karl Heinrich von Kienle completed his Habilitation under Hermann Güntert at Heidelberg by 1934. He held positions at Heidelberg University (1934, 1940), the University of Hamburg (1941–1946), and the Free University of Berlin (1953–1974).

Richard Keith Sprigg was a linguist and Tibetologist who was educated at Oakham School (~1936–1940). He held long-term academic posts at the University of London and SOAS University of London (~1948–1982).

Richard Kieckhefer specializes in religious studies and history. He studied at Saint Louis University (~1963–1967), the University of Texas at Austin (PhD ~1967–1972), and Monumenta Germaniae Historica. In 1975, he became a professor at Northwestern University.

Richard King works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Dalhousie, McGill, and Lancaster (PhD ~1988–1992) under Daniel Mariau. He held posts at the universities of Stirling (~1992–1999), Vanderbilt (~2003–2011), and Glasgow (~2011–2013).
Richard Kühnau was an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Breslau (1878–1885), where he studied under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Alfred Hillebrandt.

Richard Lionel Spittel was active in Indology. He was educated at Royal College, Colombo, and Ceylon Medical College (~1900–1905), later serving as a lecturer at Ceylon Medical College (~1910–1935) and at the National Hospital of Sri Lanka in 1910.

Indologist Richard Löbbecke studied at Marburg, Göttingen under Kielhorn and Andreas, Berlin under Pischel, Geldner, Sieg, and Huth, and Leipzig (PhD ~1904–1908) under Ernst Windisch, Bruno Lindner, and August Conrady.

Richard M. Jaffe is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He held a post at North Carolina State University (~1995–2000) before joining Duke University around 2000 as Professor of Religious Studies.

Richard Morris worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics, studying at Battersea Training College (~1851–1853). He held posts at King's College School (1869), Royal Masonic School for Boys (1875–1888), and Dedham Grammar School (~1888–1894).
